title: Foot Pain
diagnosis: Likely diagnoses may include traumatic injuries, neuropathies, or arthritis. However, a definitive diagnosis will require further investigation.
correct_orders: Obtain radiographs of the foot to assess for fractures, dislocations, or degenerative changes
Order blood tests (complete blood count, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and C-reactive protein) to evaluate for systemic inflammation
should_avoid: Prescribe nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) without a definitive diagnosis

rationale.Obtain radiographs of the foot: To identify any fractures, dislocations, or degenerative changes that may indicate underlying conditions such as osteoarthritis.
rationale.Order blood tests (complete blood count,: To evaluate for systemic inflammation, which can be associated with a variety of conditions causing foot pain.
rationale.Prescribe nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory: Since the diagnosis is unknown, it's important to avoid administering NSAIDs as they may provide temporary relief but could mask underlying pathologies that require specific treatments.
rationale.Oxygen: The patient is experiencing foot pain, which may indicate an issue requiring immediate attention. Oxygen is essential to help maintain adequate oxygenation levels in case of hypoxia.
rationale.IV access ×2 large-bore: Intravenous access is necessary for administering medications, fluids, and other life-saving interventions.

Alert and oriented unless perfusion or metabolic derangement present.
No acute rash; capillary refill and perfusion assessed.
